title: While Through This Changing World We Roam
description: While Through This Changing World We Roam in Tonic Solfa to ST. PETER, doh is Eb: the solfa with the words, staff notation, 4 verses and a piano.
about: James Montgomery wrote these words. They were printed in Hymns for Christian Devotion, compiled by John G. Adams and Edwin H. Chapin (Boston, 1846), as hymn 517 of its twenty-second edition (1853), “"Looking for another country, that is an heavenly."”.
The book printed the words without tunes, marked Common Metre (8.6.8.6), to be sung to any tune of that metre. This page sets them to ST. PETER; any other Common Metre tune fits them as well.
underlay: While through this chang-ing world we roam, From in-fan-cy to age, Heaven is the Chris-tian pil-grim's home, His rest at ev-ery stage.

lines: While through this changing world we roam,
Heaven is the Christian pilgrim's home,
While here he kneels in prayer.
Oh! there may we our treasure place,
There let our hearts be found;
That still, where sin abounded, grace
Ere long, we eye to eye shall see,
And know as we are known.

licence: Public domain: James Montgomery died in 1854.
credits: Words by James Montgomery (1771–1854), public domain, as printed in Hymns for Christian Devotion (1853); set to ST. PETER by NoteFusion, as words-only hymn books were sung.
